title: Build a profile and portfolio
summary: How to show your work so a stranger trusts you in under one minute.

slides.say: Lesson three. Clients do not know you. In less than one minute they decide if they trust you. Your profile and your portfolio must answer that question.

pts: One sentence: what you do and for whom
slides.say: A strong profile has a clear photo, your real name, and one sentence that says what you do and for whom. Add your languages and tools. Keep it simple and honest, with no exaggeration.

slides.h:
No experience?
Create your own samples.
slides.say: No experience yet? Create your own samples. Choose three imaginary clients and do the work for them. Samples you made yourself are enough to start.

pts: What was the goal? What did you do?
Easy to open on a phone
slides.say: Your portfolio needs three to five of your best samples. For each one, write a short description. What was the goal, and what did you do. And make sure it opens easily on a phone.

pts: A free page or simple website
A short link you can send
slides.say: Put it online in a free page or a simple website, and on your profile on freelance platforms. Keep one short link that you can send to any client.

pts: Do not copy other people's work
Do not invent clients or reviews
slides.say: Never fake it. Do not copy other people's work, and do not invent clients or reviews. Honesty builds long term trust, and platforms close accounts that cheat.

slides.h:
Show real work.
Explain it clearly.
slides.say: Show real work and explain it clearly. This week, create three samples and put them online. Next lesson: how to find your first client and write a proposal.
